_meta.indication: ANNOVERA is indicated for use by females of reproductive potential to prevent pregnancy; has not been adequately studied in females with a BMI >29 kg/m2.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single arm, prospective, uncontrolled trial conducted at 15 US sites
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy, sexually active women with regular menses 18-40.0 years old
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pearl Index for women ≤ 35 years of age derived from all cycles from which no back-up contraception was used
pivotal_trials.result: Pearl Index (≤ 35 yrs, using evaluable cycles within 7 days from CVS removal) 3.10 (95% CI 1.87, 4.84); 19 pregnancies in 7970 evaluable cycles

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single arm, prospective, uncontrolled global trial (8 countries, 12 sites)
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy, sexually active women with regular menses 18-40.8 years old
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pearl Index for women ≤ 35 years of age derived from all cycles in which no back-up contraception was used
pivotal_trials.result: Pearl Index (≤ 35 yrs, using evaluable cycles within 7 days from CVS removal) 2.89 (95% CI 1.79, 4.41); 21 pregnancies in 9457 evaluable cycles

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): headache/migraine (38.6%), nausea/vomiting (25.0%), vulvovaginal mycotic infection/candidiasis (14.5%), abdominal pain (13.3%), dysmenorrhea (12.5%). Serious: four VTEs (2 DVT, 1 PE, 1 cerebral venous thrombosis); VTE incidence 24.1 per 10,000 woman-years.
target_moa: Combined hormonal contraceptive (segesterone acetate, a progestin, plus ethinyl estradiol) that lowers the risk of pregnancy primarily by suppressing ovulation.
modality: Small molecule hormones (progestin segesterone acetate + estrogen ethinyl estradiol) delivered by a vaginal system/ring

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: Cigarette smoking and serious cardiovascular events — smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular events from CHC use, particularly in females over 35 years of age; CHCs should not be used by females over 35 who smoke.

rems.type: DRISK and DBRUP agreed a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of Annovera outweigh its risks; labeling is sufficient.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was conducted for this application; no issues required expert input.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under a Standard review classification.

summary.text: Annovera was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA relying on FDA's finding of safety for ethinyl estradiol and published literature, with standard review; substantial evidence of effectiveness derived from two uncontrolled Phase 3 trials (300A and 300B) and it was approved without accelerated approval or expedited-program designations.

citations.quote: The marketing application will be a 505(b)(2) application using the FDA's finding of safety for EE exposure in the CVS (through comparative BA bridging study with a listed drug COC) and published literature.
Substantial evidence of effectiveness was demonstrated in two large, multicenter, uncontrolled Phase 3 trials.

requirement.text: 3454-1: A controlled, non-interventional, long-term cohort study of new users to assess the risk for fatal and non-fatal venous thromboembolism and arterial thromboembolism associated with short- and long-term use of the product.

citations.quote: 3454-1 A controlled, non-interventional, long-term cohort study that follows a series of cohorts comprising new users of your product (segestosterone acetate and ethinyl estradiol vaginal system), new users of other vaginal ring contraceptives, new users of any intrauterine system, and new users of combined oral contraceptives containing other progestins. The primary objective of the study is to assess the risk for fatal and non-fatal venous thromboembolism and arterial thromboembolism associated with short-term and long-term use of your product in a study population representative of actual users of the product in the US and other countries where your vaginal system is prescribed.
